subject.title: fix(agents): prevent duplicate subagent recovery after restart

question: Should the at-most-once invariant live in this PR's scheduler-wide single-flight chain or in the per-session dispatch claim proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103823?
rationale: Both open PRs address the same race at different ownership boundaries, and merging both would duplicate policy; choosing the permanent concurrency boundary requires maintainer judgment about recovery lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Use dispatch-boundary ownership
options.body: Prefer one per-session claim plus a fresh authoritative store check, then close or supersede the scheduler-wide implementation after equivalent retry and restart proof.

options.title: Use scheduler single-flight
options.body: Land this PR after rebase and real restart proof, then close the competing PR and document why every production recovery entry point must pass through this scheduler.

options.title: Pause both candidates
options.body: Keep both PRs open until a maintainer-driven live restart comparison demonstrates which design preserves retries, follow-ups, and later restart recovery most safely.

recommendation.title: Use dispatch-boundary ownership
recommendation.body: Prefer one per-session claim plus a fresh authoritative store check, then close or supersede the scheduler-wide implementation after equivalent retry and restart proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior originated in their merged orphan-recovery implementation, making them the strongest available history-based owner for the lifecycle-boundary choice.
